text:
tara: Heads-up — noticed a regression in perceived streaming latency on canary (rows of users reporting slower 'start-of-text'). p95 for first-token now ~220ms vs 120ms baseline. can someone sanity-check?

sam: saw that too. initial guess: kernel fallback to fp16-path on some model shards plus our new default chunking bumped flush interval. i have a short profile.

ajay: is this the same kv-cache change we deployed yesterday? i remember a subtle handshake that can add a 1-2 token wait if the prefix cache miss path triggers.

sam: yup KvCache miss + kernel path mismatch. when microbatch size increases, we accidentally route some requests to the 'compat' kernel which has a 30-50ms per-step overhead. multiplies across tokens.

oliver: throwing telemetry snippet from the canary run:
```
model: rdx-3b-q4
workers: 8
canary-config: microbatch_max=32, stream_flush_ms=40, token_chunk=6
first_token_latency_p50/p95/p99: 80/220/420 ms
per-token_emit_p50/p95: 10/60 ms
kv_cache_miss_rate: 2.1%
kernel_switch_rate: 7.8%
```

tara: 7.8% kernel_switch_rate is the smoking gun. we used to be <1% on mainline. why did that go up?

sam: root cause — scheduler coalescing changed grouping heuristics. microbatch_max=32 caused more cross-shard requests that don't match compiled kernel layouts (seq-len/beam). fallback kicks in.

ajay: so tradeoff: larger microbatches = better throughput but higher kernel mismatch -> worse first-token p95. can we do hybrid: allow large microbatches for cold paths but force small microbatches for streaming prefix?

sam: agree, and we can prioritize kernel affinity in the router. quick experiment: reduce stream_flush_ms to 20ms and token_chunk to 4, keep microbatch_max=24. i ran a local sim: first_token_p95 drops to 140ms, overall throughput only -6%.

perf-bot: nightly-run #4721 (canary subset):
- baseline (master): first_token_p95=118ms, tokens/s=5400
- canary-old: first_token_p95=220ms, tokens/s=6800
- canary-experiment: first_token_p95=142ms, tokens/s=6400
regression_alert: severity=medium (perceived latency impact)

oliver: those numbers look promising. but we need to watch p99 too — users notice long tails. any idea why p99 remains high even after lowering chunk size?

sam: p99 tied to a couple of factors: KV-cache write stalls on heavy prefix update, and occasional kernel JIT path compile on new seq-len combos. we should prewarm kernels for common seq lengths in canary region.

ajay: actionable plan:
1) router: add kernel-affinity tag for streaming requests (prefer kernels compiled for short seq).
2) flush policy: stream_flush_ms default -> 20ms for real-time tier, token_chunk default -> 4.
3) microbatch cap: lower to 24 for streams; keep 32-ish for batch-only endpoints.
4) prewarm: schedule kernel precompile for seq lengths [16,32,64] during deployment window.
5) telemetry: add metric "perceived_start_latency_ms" which measures time-to-first-chunk + client-threshold (50ms).

tara: can we roll these as a canary A/B? oliver, sam — how long for the router change and new defaults?

oliver: router affinity change is a small patch (1 day + e2e). flush/default tweaks are just config (hot deploy). prewarm needs a bit more infra (~3 days to add background compile job).

sam: i'll push a config-only canary today with stream_flush_ms=20 and token_chunk=4 and microbatch_max=24 for the realtime route. enable kernel-affinity=false initially, then flip after we validate p99.

perf-bot: canary-deploy #885 started. target: 10% traffic in us-west. will report 1h and 24h snapshots.

tara: perfect. also please add a short test in perf-suite that asserts kernel_switch_rate < 2% under streaming load. if it fails we shouldn't rollout.

ajay: adding that to test matrix now.

sam: quick note for docs: mention tradeoff explicitly — throughput boost from bigger microbatches can hide kernel mismatch regressions that hurt perceived latency for streaming. add to release notes.

tara: ok thanks. ping me if p95 doesn't drop in the canary. :thumbsup:

oliver: will monitor. updating tickets and linking perf graphs.

sam: filing follow-up to prewarm and router affinity.

perf-bot: canary snapshot (1h): first_token_p95=148ms, first_token_p99=310ms, kernel_switch_rate=2.4%, tokens/s=6300

tara: nice improvement. leaving this open until prewarm lands and p99 improves.

ajay: noted. closing loop once prewarm shows p99 < 220ms on 24h canary.

oliver: ack.
